notes_for_editor: (1) Thin station. No keepers, no wrecks, no storms and no pre-1991 history for the outer pair turned up in the sources read: the Canadian Marine annual reports (1900-1924, the corpus) list a 'Summerside Harbour Back Range Light' and a 'Summerside Wharf' but no outer range at Summerside. The story is short on purpose. (2) Range: the Coast Guard's List of Lights gives 16 nautical miles; the PEI Lighthouse Society gives a nominal range of 18 nautical miles. Both are stated in the story as 'the sources differ'. Not corrected; check the current List of Lights. (3) Ownership: the record says federal. The PEI Lighthouse Society and Rowlett both report a City of Summerside petition or application for ownership under the Heritage Lighthouse Program. The status of that application is unknown and should be checked before publication. (4) The record's coordinates (46.395312, -63.809751) match the Coast Guard's front-light position to within about 3 m (46 23 43.1 N, 63 48 35.0 W). (5) Erosion reinforcement (the Society) is undated and not in the story's timeline. (6) The rear light's details come from Rowlett and the Coast Guard list. Coast Guard entry 1018.2 gives focal height 14.9 m, tower 10.1 m, range 17 nautical miles; LighthouseFriends gives focal 14.8 m and tower 10.1 m; Rowlett gives focal 15 m (49 ft) and tower 10 m (33 ft). The story gives Rowlett's figures, attributed. The Society's rear-light page was not read. (7) The Parks Canada Directory of Federal Heritage Designations was not checked for this light. (8) Wikipedia and Grokipedia were not used as sources. (9) The 'Summerside Back Range' story (data/stories/ca-pe-summerside-back-range.md) covers the inner pair and was not used as a source. (10) The inner range and the Indian Head light are mentioned only as the Rowlett and LighthouseFriends entries state them.
